claims.claim: Concomitant with changes in levels, junction configuration and architecture are also compromised, which are not always captured by intensity measurements.
claims.source: Concomitant with changes in levels, junction configuration and architecture are also compromised, which are not always captured by intensity measurements.
claims.evidence: Stated as an observation motivating the need for new parameters.

claims.claim: Junction Mapper builds from quantitative analysis of images from RNAi screens.
claims.source: We designed and validated a semi-automated system (Figure 2), Junction Mapper, that builds from our quantitative analysis of images from RNAi screens (Erasmus et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Stated with citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Junction Mapper implements novel quantification tools including corners, length and area.
claims.source: Junction Mapper implements novel quantification tools (corners, length and area) and a variety of novel primary and secondary parameters expressed per individual junction.
claims.evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claims.claim: The main advantage of Junction Mapper is to efficiently segment junctions in a variety of cell types and of different junction patterns, from linear to fragmented or disrupted contacts.
claims.source: The main advantage of Junction Mapper is to efficiently segment junctions in a variety of cell types and of different junction patterns, from linear to fragmented or disrupted contacts.
claims.evidence: Stated as the main advantage of the software.

claims.claim: The software detects the contacting interface between two cells and obtains a skeletonized edge map.
claims.source: The software detects the contacting interface between two cells and obtains a skeletonized edge map (summarised stepwise in Figure 2—figure supplement 1; see Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: Stated as a capability and referenced to supplementary figure.

claims.claim: Users can adjust the outline manually by removing incorrect or adding missing lines, with subsequent refinement of the line location and geometry by the software algorithm.
claims.source: Although semi-automated, users can adjust the outline manually by removing incorrect or adding missing lines, with subsequent refinement of the line location and geometry by the software algorithm (detailed in Appendix 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claims.claim: A dilation step is applied to define the area to be quantified around the skeletonized map.
claims.source: A dilation step is applied (user controlled) to define the area to be quantified around the skeletonized map (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a step in the software workflow.

claims.claim: The software automatically identifies each cell–cell corner.
claims.source: To identify individual junctions for further quantification, the software then automatically identifies each cell–cell corner (i.e. point of contact between three or more cells, see its mathematical definition in Appendix 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a capability of the software.

claims.claim: The number and location of corners in each cell can be manually adjusted by the user.
claims.source: The number and location of corners in each cell can also be manually adjusted by the user (Appendix 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claims.claim: Images obtained at different resolutions can be used for analyses in Junction Mapper.
claims.source: Images obtained at different resolutions can be used for analyses in Junction Mapper (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a capability with reference to supplementary file.

claims.claim: For defining the automated skeletonized edge of each image, a suitable signal-to-noise ratio is necessary to ensure enough contrast to differentiate staining at junctions from the cytoplasm.
claims.source: For defining the automated skeletonized edge of each image, a suitable signal-to-noise ratio is necessary to ensure enough contrast to differentiate staining at junctions from the cytoplasm (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Stated as a requirement and supported by figure.

claims.claim: For efficient skeleton definition the Peak Signal to Noise ratio should be above 22 dB.
claims.source: For efficient skeleton definition the ratio should be above 22 dB (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Stated as a threshold value and supported by figure.

claims.claim: The higher the fragmentation of junctions in the image, the more user input is necessary to define the final skeleton outline for quantification.
claims.source: The higher the fragmentation of junctions in the image, the more user input is necessary to define the final skeleton outline for quantification.
claims.evidence: Stated as an observation about software usage.

claims.claim: The measurement of the different parameters is performed simultaneously and automatically, in an unbiased manner.
claims.source: The measurement of the different parameters is performed simultaneously and automatically, in an unbiased manner (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claims.claim: The output per junction is produced as an Excel file that contains the selected image, skeleton and the quantification of pre-designed measurements and parameters.
claims.source: The output per junction is produced as an Excel file that contains the selected image, skeleton and the quantification of pre-designed measurements and parameters (see below).
claims.evidence: Stated as a feature of the software output.

claims.claim: Different phenotypes of junction perturbation may require a distinct set of parameters to appropriately capture the disruption features.
claims.source: We envisage that different phenotypes of junction perturbation may require a distinct set of parameters to appropriately capture the disruption features (Figure 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a rationale for the parameter design.

claims.claim: Interface is the contacting membrane between two neighbouring cells and delimited by cell–cell corners.
claims.source: Interface is the contacting membrane between two neighbouring cells and delimited by cell–cell corners.
claims.evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claims.claim: A cell–cell contact or junction is the region of the interface covered by adhesion receptors.
claims.source: A cell–cell contact or junction is the region of the interface covered by adhesion receptors (e.g. cadherin staining).
claims.evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claims.claim: Junctions may or may not extend to the whole of the interface (corner-to-corner), and can appear fragmented or dotted.
claims.source: Junctions may or may not extend to the whole of the interface (corner-to-corner), and can appear fragmented or dotted (Figure 1, Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: Stated as an observation and supported by figures.

claims.claim: Area is the dilated region around the skeleton and is set to encompass the width of a junctional marker staining.
claims.source: Area is the dilated region around the skeleton and is set to encompass the width of a junctional marker staining (which can vary in thickness).
claims.evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claims.claim: Contour is the length measurement of the outline of the skeleton between defined points (interface or junction).
claims.source: Contour is the length measurement of the outline of the skeleton between defined points (interface or junction).
claims.evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claims.claim: The straight-line length is defined as the shortest distance (Euclidian distance) between corners that form the boundaries of one junction or interface.
claims.source: Finally, the straight-line length is defined as the shortest distance (Euclidian distance) between corners that form the boundaries of one junction or interface.
claims.evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claims.claim: The primary parameters were validated to assess measurements were as predicted from their definition.
claims.source: The primary parameters were validated to assess measurements were as predicted from their definition.
claims.evidence: Stated as a validation approach.

claims.claim: Junction contour and area were more severely disrupted when two neighbouring cells contained exogenous H-RasG12V.
claims.source: Measurements of the primary parameters (Figure 3) confirmed that junction contour and area were more severely disrupted when two neighbouring cells contained exogenous H-RasG12V (Figure 4D–E).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: The interface of mosaic contacts shared by expressing and non-expressing cells (en) were not significantly different from controls.
claims.source: The interface of mosaic contacts shared by expressing and non-expressing cells (en) were not significantly different from controls (Figure 4B,C,F).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: Increasing the dilation values modifies the area-based but not the length-based measurements.
claims.source: Increasing the dilation values modifies the area-based (D) but not the length-based measurements (C).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: Larger dilation values obtained higher VE-cadherin area measurements at the undulated contacts.
claims.source: Larger dilation values obtained higher VE-cadherin area measurements at the undulated contacts (H).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: Increasing thresholding levels did not interfere with interface contour length, as it is defined by the position of corners.
claims.source: Increasing thresholding levels did not interfere with interface contour length, as it is defined by the position of corners (C).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: The fragmented junction length was reduced by increasing thresholding.
claims.source: The fragmented junction length was reduced by increasing thresholding (C), similar to what was observed with the E-cadherin area and intensity (D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: The primary parameters measure the length and area of various features as predicted and are selectively modulated by user-controlled settings in accordance to their definition.
claims.source: Taken together, we concluded that the primary parameters measure the length and area of various features as predicted and are selectively modulated by user-controlled settings in accordance to their definition (Appendix 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion from validation experiments.

claims.claim: The Linearity Index measures how straight an interface between two cells is.
claims.source: The Linearity Index measures how straight an interface between two cells is, as proposed by Takeichi and colleagues (Otani et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: Stated as a parameter definition with citation.

claims.claim: Coverage Index is a length measurement of the percentage of the interface length that is covered by the junction marker staining.
claims.source: Coverage Index is a length measurement of the percentage of the interface length that is covered by the junction marker staining and has been previously used manually in the lab (Lozano et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Stated as a parameter definition with citation.

claims.claim: Interface Occupancy measures the area occupied by the marker within the Interface Area of each junction.
claims.source: First, Interface Occupancy, measures the area occupied by the marker within the Interface Area of each junction.
claims.evidence: Stated as a parameter definition.

claims.claim: Junction Protein Intensity per Interface area calculates the fluorescence intensity within the Interface Area.
claims.source: Second, Junction Protein Intensity per Interface area calculates the fluorescence intensity within the Interface Area.
claims.evidence: Stated as a parameter definition.

claims.claim: Cluster Density is the junction protein intensity level within the area delimited by its staining.
claims.source: Finally, Cluster Density is the junction protein intensity level within the area delimited by its staining (i.e. Fragmented Junction Area, which considers any fragmentation of the staining; additional parameters are described in Appendix 2).
claims.evidence: Stated as a parameter definition.

claims.claim: The Coverage Index parameter calculated by Junction Mapper was validated by manual quantification using FIJI on cells expressing active Rac1.
claims.source: The Coverage Index parameter calculated by Junction Mapper was validated by manual quantification using FIJI on cells expressing active Rac1 (Supplementary file 2A-B).
claims.evidence: Stated as a validation approach.

claims.claim: Using either quantification, manual or Junction Mapper, a significant statistical difference was observed between values of control and Rac1-expressing cells.
claims.source: Using either quantification, manual or Junction Mapper, a significant statistical difference was observed between values of control and Rac1-expressing cells (Supplementary file 2C).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: Lower values were obtained with the manual quantification method as predicted when using straight-lines for measurement.
claims.source: Lower values were obtained with the manual quantification method as predicted when using straight-lines for measurement.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: When controls values were compared between the two methods, no statistical difference was obtained.
claims.source: However, when controls values were compared between the two methods, no statistical difference was obtained (Supplementary file 2C).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: The reproducibility of secondary parameters was assessed in independent biological replicates by the same user.
claims.source: Thus, the parameters give results as expected from previous manual methods. In addition, the reproducibility of secondary parameters was assessed in independent biological replicates by the same user.
claims.evidence: Stated as a validation approach.

claims.claim: Across biological replicates of cells overexpressing active Rac1, the absolute values obtained for each sample were slightly different.
claims.source: Across biological replicates of cells overexpressing active Rac1, the absolute values obtained for each sample were slightly different (Scheme 1B-D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by scheme.

claims.claim: The overall result is the same between replicates: a reduction of Coverage Index and Interface Occupancy of E-cadherin at junctions from Rac1 expressing cells.
claims.source: However, the overall result is the same between replicates: a reduction of Coverage Index and Interface Occupancy of E-cadherin at junctions from Rac1 expressing cells (Scheme 1B-D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by scheme.

claims.claim: Comparison of control values between biological replicates (or between Rac1 expressing cells) was not statistically different.
claims.source: Comparison of control values between biological replicates (or between Rac1 expressing cells) was not statistically different.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claims.claim: Confluent epithelial monolayers with clearly defined junctions and corners produced less output variability from different users than images with disrupted contacts.
claims.source: Confluent epithelial monolayers with clearly defined junctions and corners produced less output variability from different users than images with disrupted contacts (Supplementary file 3A-D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claims.claim: A particular hot spot for differences was the identification of cell corners in disrupted contacts, where corners are often not covered by cadherin staining.
claims.source: We found that a particular hot spot for differences was the identification of cell corners in disrupted contacts, where corners are often not covered by cadherin staining (Supplementary file 3B).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claims.claim: Pair-wise comparison of primary parameters of matched epithelial junctions obtained independently by two users showed significant differences.
claims.source: Second, pair-wise comparison of primary parameters of matched epithelial junctions obtained independently by two users showed significant differences (Supplementary file 3C-D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claims.claim: When secondary parameters were calculated, the profiles obtained by the two users were similar, aside the absolute values being different.
claims.source: However, when secondary parameters were calculated, the profiles obtained by the two users were similar, aside the absolute values being different (Supplementary file 3E-F, see also Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claims.claim: User bias can be minimized by using secondary parameters and normalizing to controls in each replicate.
claims.source: We conclude that, in addition to the impact of dilation and thresholding settings, Junction Mapper results are impacted by user influence on the cell edge map. This influence is stronger in cell images with disrupted cell–cell contacts, where higher frequency of inaccurate corner and skeleton detection occurs. Hence more manual edge correction is required the more robust secondary parameter measurements should be considered. Furthermore, absolute comparisons can not be made between experiments. Instead, normalization of secondary parameters to controls in each replicate will facilitate comparisons.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion from user-bias validation.

claims.claim: Junction perturbation occurs more efficiently between two RacQ61L-expressing neighbouring keratinocytes.
claims.source: Previous visual analysis indicated that perturbation of cell–cell contacts occurs more efficiently between two RacQ61L-expressing neighbouring keratinocytes (Braga et al., 1997; Lozano et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Oncogenic H-Ras expression induces a longer contacting interface between cells and a progressive fragmentation of E-cadherin staining.
claims.source: Based on the quantification of the primary parameters, oncogenic H-Ras expression induces a longer contacting interface between cells and a progressive fragmentation of E-cadherin staining.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the data analysis.

claims.claim: Active Src expression did not promote elongation of the contacting interface or an increase in interface area.
claims.source: For example, active Src expression did not promote elongation of the contacting interface or an increase in interface area (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H–I), while active Rac1 did not induce fragmentation of cadherin staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: Active Rac1 did not induce fragmentation of cadherin staining.
claims.source: For example, active Src expression did not promote elongation of the contacting interface or an increase in interface area (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H–I), while active Rac1 did not induce fragmentation of cadherin staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: Distinct subsets of parameters can differentiate alterations by different stimuli, thereby providing a unique disruption profile.
claims.source: The above data may indicate that distinct subsets of parameters can differentiate alterations by different stimuli, thereby providing a unique disruption profile (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: The undulation of the interface was increased among cells expressing H-RasG12V or SrcY527F when compared to controls.
claims.source: When compared to controls, the undulation of the interface was increased among cells expressing H-RasG12V or SrcY527F (higher Interface Linearity Index, Figure 5B,D), but remained unchanged for Rac1Q61L-perturbed junctions (ee, Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: The undulation of the interface remained unchanged for Rac1Q61L-perturbed junctions.
claims.source: When compared to controls, the undulation of the interface was increased among cells expressing H-RasG12V or SrcY527F (higher Interface Linearity Index, Figure 5B,D), but remained unchanged for Rac1Q61L-perturbed junctions (ee, Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: As E-cadherin is removed from junctions, the interface between H-RasG12V and SrcY527F expressing cells becomes less tensile.
claims.source: These data indicate that, as E-cadherin is removed from junctions, the interface between H-RasG12V and SrcY527F expressing cells becomes less tensile.
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: The percentage of the interface area occupied by E-cadherin receptors was decreased in all samples expressing activated oncogenes.
claims.source: The percentage of the interface area occupied by E-cadherin receptors was decreased in all samples (Interface Occupancy, Figure 5B,F), but did not reach significance in Src-expressing cells (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: The intensity levels of cadherin at junctions was significantly reduced following transfection of activated H-Ras or Src.
claims.source: The intensity levels of cadherin at junctions was significantly reduced following transfection of activated H-Ras or Src when measured as raw values (E-cadherin Intensity) or corrected per contacting area between two cells (E-cadherin Intensity per Interface Area) (Figure 5B,D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: After active Rac1 expression, neither E-cadherin Intensity nor E-cadherin Intensity per Interface Area was significantly changed.
claims.source: In contrast, after active Rac1 expression, neither parameter was significantly changed.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: The density of cadherin clusters was decreased in H-RasG12V and SrcY527F, but slightly augmented in RacQ61L.
claims.source: Consistent with the distinct phenotype of junction perturbation seen in Rac1Q61L-transfected cells, the density of cadherin clusters was decreased in H-RasG12V and SrcY527F, but slightly augmented in RacQ61L.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: Activated Rac1 does not significantly reduce the overall levels of E-cadherin at junctions.
claims.source: Our preliminary observations suggest that activated Rac1 does not significantly reduce the overall levels of E-cadherin at junctions, since receptor intensity at the interface area is not reduced.
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: Rac1 activation progressively redistributes receptors at the junction, maintaining straight, linear junctions.
claims.source: Rather, Rac1 activation progressively redistributes receptors at the junction (reduced Interface Occupancy and higher Cluster Density), maintaining straight, linear junctions.
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: Activated H-Ras or Src disrupt junctions via fragmentation and removal of E-cadherin consistently throughout the contacting interface.
claims.source: In contrast, activated H-Ras or Src disrupt junctions via fragmentation and removal of E-cadherin consistently throughout the contacting interface (decreased in Interface Occupancy and Cluster Density), with concomitant undulation of cell–cell contacts (i.e. reduced tension or stiffness at junctions).
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: Depletion of CIP4 results in modest, but significant fluctuations in E-cadherin at junctions (20%–30%).
claims.source: Depletion of CIP4 (a regulator of cadherin trafficking) (Leibfried et al., 2008; Rolland et al., 2014), VAV2 (an exchange factor for Rho, Rac2 and Cdc42) (Vigil et al., 2010) or EEF1A (an actin bundling protein) (Mateyak and Kinzy, 2010) results in modest, but significant fluctuations in E-cadherin at junctions (20%–30%) using a thresholding method (Erasmus et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: CIP4, VAV2 or EEF1A siRNA did not interfere with the linearity of the contacting interface.
claims.source: When analysed with Junction Mapper, CIP4, VAV2 or EEF1A siRNA did not interfere with the linearity of the contacting interface (Figure 6B,D,F), in line with the appearance of normal, linear junctions.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: A small decrease in E-cadherin intensity was observed in both CIP4- and VAV2-depleted cells.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous findings (Erasmus et al., 2016), a small decrease in E-cadherin intensity was observed in both CIP4- and VAV2-depleted cells (Figure 6B,F), while EEF1A siRNA promoted the unusual phenotype of higher levels of cadherin receptors (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures and citation.

claims.claim: EEF1A siRNA promoted the unusual phenotype of higher levels of cadherin receptors.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous findings (Erasmus et al., 2016), a small decrease in E-cadherin intensity was observed in both CIP4- and VAV2-depleted cells (Figure 6B,F), while EEF1A siRNA promoted the unusual phenotype of higher levels of cadherin receptors (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: Despite the similar reduction in E-cadherin intensity levels following VAV2 and CIP4 depletion, receptors were removed in different ways from junctions.
claims.source: Strikingly, despite the similar reduction in E-cadherin intensity levels following VAV2 and CIP4 depletion, receptors were removed in different ways from junctions.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: The clusters of cadherin receptors were less dense with lower levels of CIP4.
claims.source: The clusters of cadherin receptors were less dense with lower levels of CIP4, while upon VAV2 siRNA, the density of the clusters slightly increased (Cluster density, Figure 6B,F).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: Upon VAV2 siRNA, the density of the cadherin clusters slightly increased.
claims.source: The clusters of cadherin receptors were less dense with lower levels of CIP4, while upon VAV2 siRNA, the density of the clusters slightly increased (Cluster density, Figure 6B,F).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: The discrete changes in junctions result from reduced cadherin levels throughout the contacting interface by lower density of receptor clusters (CIP4 RNAi) or localised E-cadherin removal and redistribution into denser clusters (VAV2 RNAi).
claims.source: Thus, the discrete changes in junctions result from reduced cadherin levels throughout the contacting interface by lower density of receptor clusters (CIP4 RNAi) or localised E-cadherin removal and redistribution into denser clusters (VAV2 RNAi; Figure 6B,F).
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: EEF1A depletion augmented E-cadherin Intensity and Cluster Density along the interface.
claims.source: In contrast, EEF1A depletion augmented E-cadherin Intensity and Cluster Density along the interface.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: Junction Mapper can detect phenotypes reproducibly and with good dynamic range.
claims.source: Taken together, these data highlight the ability of the Junction Mapper to detect phenotypes reproducibly and with good dynamic range.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the data analysis.

claims.claim: Thrombin is a serine protease that stimulates protease-activated receptor (PAR) in endothelial cells to increase vascular permeability in inflammation and injury.
claims.source: Thrombin is a serine protease that stimulates protease-activated receptor (PAR) in endothelial cells to increase vascular permeability in inflammation and injury (Figure 7A) (Kumar et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: There were no significant changes in the Interface Linearity Index in thrombin-treated endothelial cells.
claims.source: There were no significant changes in the Interface Linearity Index (Figure 7A,B), consistent with the limitation of Junction Mapper to skeletonize zig-zagged junctions and thus measure their length (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–F).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: In thrombin-treated cells, VE-cadherin distribution along the interface area (Interface Occupancy), intensity of VE-cadherin staining and normalised intensity per contacting interface were substantially higher.
claims.source: However, with appropriate dilation values (Supplementary file 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), alterations were detected for area-based measurements. In thrombin-treated cells, VE-cadherin distribution along the interface area (Interface Occupancy), intensity of VE-cadherin staining and normalised intensity per contacting interface were substantially higher (Figure 7C–E).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: The density of VE-cadherin clusters was enhanced upon treatment with thrombin.
claims.source: The density of VE-cadherin clusters was also enhanced upon treatment with thrombin (Figure 7F), implying that a higher number of receptors is recruited per contact area.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claims.claim: The increased levels of VE-cadherin at junctions may promote stronger endothelial adhesion, which is relevant to sustain elevated intracellular tension and contractility induced by thrombin stimulation.
claims.source: Using area-based parameters, we find that the contacting interface is occupied more efficiently, with higher density of VE-cadherin receptors at endothelial junctions upon thrombin treatment. Thus, it seems that the increased levels of VE-cadherin at junctions may promote stronger endothelial adhesion, which is relevant to sustain elevated intracellular tension and contractility induced by thrombin stimulation.
claims.evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claims.claim: These results are consistent with the role of mechanical tension in receptor modulation and integrity of multicellular tissues.
claims.source: These results are consistent with the role of mechanical tension in receptor modulation and integrity of multicellular tissues (Liu et al., 2010), and merit further experimentation.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: At steady state, in control cardiomyocytes, intercalated discs have clusters of cadherin receptors that are far apart.
claims.source: At steady state, our data show that, in control cardiomyocytes, intercalated discs have clusters of cadherin receptors that are far apart.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: Hypertrophic stimulus in cellulo (neonatal rat cardiomyocytes) potently increases the levels of β-catenin at contacting interfaces.
claims.source: Hypertrophic stimulus in cellulo (neonatal rat cardiomyocytes) potently increases the levels of β-catenin at contacting interfaces, consistent with what was reported in hamster and human hypertrophic hearts (Masuelli et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claims.claim: Connexin 43 total protein and mRNA levels are augmented by hypertrophic signals in cellulo.
claims.source: Connexin 43 is a major connexin isoform found in cardiomyocytes and its total protein and mRNA levels are augmented by hypertrophic signals in cellulo (i.e. phenylephrine) (Salameh et al., 2008; Stanbouly et al., 2008) or in human hearts with compensated left-ventricular hypertrophy by pressure-overloading (Kostin et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The formation of gap junctions is enhanced after hypertrophy stimulation in cellulo.
claims.source: The initial profiling analysis with Junction Mapper suggest that the formation of gap junctions is enhanced after hypertrophy stimulation in cellulo, confirming the broadening of intercalated disc area and higher number of GAP junctions in compensated hypertrophic hearts of human patients (Kostin et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claims.claim: Although hypertrophic stimulus increases both β-catenin and connexin 43 levels at intercalated discs, these markers are regulated in distinct ways.
claims.source: Although hypertrophic stimulus increases both β-catenin and connexin 43 levels at intercalated discs, these markers are regulated in distinct ways.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: The β-catenin cluster density is decreased leading to a more contiguous distribution after hypertrophic stimulus.
claims.source: The β-catenin cluster density is decreased leading to a more contiguous distribution, while connexin 43 is localised in clusters of higher density.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: Connexin 43 is localised in clusters of higher density after hypertrophic stimulus.
claims.source: The β-catenin cluster density is decreased leading to a more contiguous distribution, while connexin 43 is localised in clusters of higher density.
claims.evidence: Stated as a result.

claims.claim: The most innovative aspects of Junction Mapper are the measurement of receptor density and occupancy, the automatic quantification of fragmented staining at a junction, and the correlation of the parameters from two junctional markers along the same junction.
claims.source: The most innovative aspects of Junction Mapper are, first, the measurement of receptor density and occupancy, via the normalization of the junction marker intensity, length and area to the available contacting interface and cell–cell contact area. Second, the automatic quantification of fragmented staining at a junction, which has not been feasible previously and, third, the correlation of the parameters from two junctional markers along the same junction.
claims.evidence: Stated as the innovative aspects of the software.

claims.claim: Machine learning algorithms have the potential to improve and automate segmentation success, especially of highly fragmented contacts.
claims.source: Machine learning algorithms certainly have the potential to improve and automate segmentation success, especially of highly fragmented contacts.
claims.evidence: Stated as a future direction.

claims.claim: The availability of training image datasets with boundaries manually-generated is still a bottleneck for machine learning algorithms.
claims.source: However, the availability of training image datasets with boundaries manually-generated is still a bottleneck (Häring et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation.

claims.claim: One possible use of the software is the generation of precise cell outline skeletons that can be used to train machine-learning algorithms in the future.
claims.source: One possible use of the software is therefore the generation of precise cell outline skeletons that can be used to train machine-learning algorithms in the future.
claims.evidence: Stated as a potential application.

claims.claim: User contribution is necessary and essential to perform the quality control of skeleton outline, corner positioning and setting up the dilation and threshold levels in a given dataset.
claims.source: While semi-automation has been implemented during the image processing by Junction Mapper, user contribution is necessary and essential to perform the quality control of skeleton outline, corner positioning and setting up the dilation and threshold levels in a given dataset.
claims.evidence: Stated as a requirement of the software.

claims.claim: User bias is particularly relevant in images with very disrupted and irregular junctions.
claims.source: User bias is particularly relevant in images with very disrupted and irregular junctions, and absolute values are not suitable for comparison across experiments in some cases.
claims.evidence: Stated as a limitation.

claims.claim: Analysis of biological replicates or independent analysis by different users show that the secondary parameters are more robust against user bias.
claims.source: However, user bias can be minimized. Analysis of biological replicates or independent analysis by different users show that (i) the secondary parameters are more robust against user bias and (ii) obtained results are similar across replicates when comparing control and treated samples.

results.result: Junction Mapper is an open-access, semi-automated software tool developed in Java that identifies cell-cell contact interfaces and corners with minimal user input, quantifies junction parameters (length, area, intensity), and uniquely measures fragmented junctions across various cell types.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C18-C20, C27-C28, and C135-C137 collectively describe the software's core capabilities and are directly stated in the manuscript with supporting figures (Figure 2). The software's availability on GitHub (C136) and its technical implementation (C135, C137) are explicitly documented in the methods section.

results.result: Junction Mapper's workflow involves automated detection of cell-cell interfaces to create a skeletonized edge map, with user-adjustable manual corrections, followed by dilation, corner identification, and automated parameter measurement. The software requires a Peak Signal to Noise ratio above 22 dB for efficient skeleton definition.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C39 describe the technical workflow and are supported by Figure 2 and supplementary figures. The PSNR threshold of 22 dB (C36) is explicitly stated and validated in Figure 2—figure supplement 2. The workflow steps are clearly documented in the methods and results sections.

results.result: Primary parameters in Junction Mapper measure fundamental junction properties including interface (contacting membrane between cells), junction (region covered by adhesion receptors), area (dilated region around skeleton), contour (length of skeleton outline), and straight-line length (Euclidian distance between corners). These parameters were validated and behave as predicted from their definitions.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C47 and C54 define the primary parameters and their validation. Figure 3 demonstrates that measurements behave as predicted, with validation experiments showing expected responses to user-controlled settings (dilation and thresholding). The validation is systematic and well-documented.

results.result: Validation experiments demonstrate that junction contour and area are more severely disrupted when two neighboring cells express H-RasG12V compared to mosaic contacts or controls. User-controlled settings (dilation and thresholding) selectively affect area-based versus length-based measurements as predicted.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C53 are supported by Figures 3 and 4, with statistical analyses showing significant differences. The validation demonstrates that dilation affects area-based but not length-based measurements (C50), and thresholding affects fragmented junction length but not interface contour (C52-C53), consistent with parameter definitions.

results.result: Secondary parameters normalize measurements to interface or junction dimensions and include Linearity Index, Coverage Index, Interface Occupancy, Junction Protein Intensity per Interface Area, and Cluster Density. These parameters were validated against manual quantification and show reproducibility across biological replicates despite slight variations in absolute values.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C67 describe secondary parameters and their validation. Scheme 1 and Supplementary file 2 demonstrate that Junction Mapper produces statistically equivalent results to manual quantification (C61), though with different absolute values due to methodological differences (C62-C63). Reproducibility across biological replicates is demonstrated (C65-C67).

results.result: User bias analysis reveals that confluent epithelial monolayers produce less variability than disrupted contacts, with corner identification being a particular source of variation. However, secondary parameters are more robust against user bias than primary parameters, and normalization to controls minimizes bias effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C72 and C115-C117 address user bias and are supported by Supplementary file 3 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1. While primary parameters show significant differences between users (C70), secondary parameters produce similar profiles (C71), supporting the conclusion that user bias can be minimized through appropriate parameter selection and normalization (C72, C117).

results.result: Junction Mapper distinguishes distinct disruption profiles among oncogenes: H-RasG12V and SrcY527F induce interface elongation, undulation, and E-cadherin fragmentation/removal with decreased cluster density, while Rac1Q61L redistributes receptors without fragmentation or undulation, maintaining straight junctions with increased cluster density.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C87 and C119-C120 describe oncogene-specific junction disruption patterns supported by Figures 4-5 and Scheme 2. However, the manuscript explicitly states these are from single technical replicates (C77) and describes findings as 'preliminary observations' (C85), requiring additional biological replicates to confirm the patterns. The mechanistic interpretations (C80, C85-C87) are speculative.

results.result: Junction Mapper detects subtle changes in junction phenotypes following siRNA depletion of cytoskeleton-associated proteins (CIP4, VAV2, EEF1A), revealing that similar reductions in E-cadherin intensity can result from distinct mechanisms: reduced cluster density (CIP4) versus localized removal with denser clusters (VAV2).
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C97 and C121-C122 are supported by Figure 6 and Scheme 3, with statistical analyses showing significant differences. The results confirm prior findings (C88, C121) while revealing new mechanistic distinctions (C92-C95). The data demonstrate the software's ability to detect both major and minor changes with good dynamic range (C97).

results.result: In thrombin-treated endothelial cells, Junction Mapper detects increased VE-cadherin distribution, intensity, and cluster density at junctions using area-based parameters, though the characteristic zig-zag pattern is not captured by automated skeleton definition. The increased VE-cadherin may promote stronger adhesion to sustain elevated tension and contractility.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C103 and C123-C124 are supported by Figure 7 with statistical significance (N=2 biological replicates). However, the software's inability to capture zig-zag patterns (C99, C124) is a significant limitation. The mechanistic interpretation about stronger adhesion (C102) is speculative and explicitly stated to 'merit further experimentation' (C103).

results.result: In cardiomyocytes, hypertrophic stimulation increases β-catenin and connexin 43 levels at intercalated discs, but through distinct mechanisms: β-catenin shows decreased cluster density with more contiguous distribution, while connexin 43 forms denser clusters, suggesting enhanced gap junction formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C110 and C125-C127 are supported by Figure 8 and Scheme 4 with statistical analyses. However, the data are from a single technical replicate, and the manuscript explicitly states 'further investigation is necessary to ascertain the profiling and biological significance' (preceding C128). The findings are consistent with prior literature (C105-C107, C126-C127) but require additional validation.

results.result: Junction Mapper successfully quantifies junctions in multiple cell types (epithelia, endothelia, cardiomyocytes) that deviate from standard epithelial phenotypes, providing unique fingerprints for different stimuli. The software has broad applicability despite limitations with highly fragmented/zig-zagged junctions and untested applications (stratified epithelia).
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C5, C21, C111, C118, and C128-C134 describe the software's broad applicability and are supported by data from multiple cell types (Figures 7-8). The limitations are explicitly acknowledged (C128-C130), and the potential applications (C131-C134) are appropriately framed as future directions. The demonstration across three distinct cell types with different junction architectures supports the broad applicability claim.

results.result: The manuscript establishes that existing quantitative image analysis methods have restricted capabilities for mammalian cell junctions, particularly for detecting non-intensity-based attributes like shape, length, fragmentation, and continuity, which motivated the development of Junction Mapper.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C17 establish the background and motivation for the study, supported by multiple citations to prior work. These claims accurately represent established knowledge about junction biology (C6-C11) and limitations of existing methods (C12-C17). The citations are appropriate and the characterization of the problem is well-supported.

results.result: Normal epithelial junctions appear as straight lines with uniformly distributed E-cadherin receptors delimited by tricellular corners, while various stimuli disrupt this architecture in different ways that are not always captured by intensity measurements alone, requiring distinct parameter sets for appropriate quantification.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C25 and C40 describe fundamental junction biology and the rationale for multiple parameters, supported by Figure 1. These observations are well-established and provide the conceptual foundation for the parameter design. The claim that different phenotypes require distinct parameters (C40) is validated throughout the results.

results.result: Junction Mapper builds upon prior quantitative analysis methods from RNAi screens developed by the same research group.
results.evaluation: Claim C26 is explicitly stated with citation to Erasmus et al., 2016, establishing the software's development history and connection to prior work by the authors.

results.result: Machine learning algorithms could improve Junction Mapper's segmentation, particularly for fragmented contacts, though training dataset availability remains a bottleneck. The software could generate training data for future machine learning applications.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C114 discuss future directions and are appropriately framed as speculation. The limitation regarding training datasets (C113) is supported by citation to Häring et al., 2018. These are reasonable assessments of future potential rather than claims about current capabilities.
